original_question: Let L be the closure on UC_b(R, R) of the differential operator (Lf)(x) = a(x)f''(x) + b(x)f'(x) + c(x)f(x), where a, b, c are bounded uniformly continuous real-valued functions and a(x) >= a_0 > 0 for all x. Find an explicitly given Chernoff function S(t) for L such that S is Chernoff-equivalent to the semigroup (e^{tL}), there exist a dense subspace D and constants M > 0, q > 1, n_0 > 0 with ||e^{tL}f - S(t/n)^n f|| <= M / q^n for all n >= n_0 and all f in D, and the formula for S(t) depends explicitly on a, b, c, f, and x without hiding the unknown semigroup inside the definition.
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 30 ("Super-fast converging Chernoff approximations example"), specifically its formal statement for the second-order operator (Lf)(x)=a(x)f''(x)+b(x)f'(x)+c(x)f(x) on UC_b(R,R), together with the adjoining comments that define "fast" and "super fast" convergence and insist on an explicit non-circular Chernoff function.
correct_elements: Your draft is aimed at the right open problem. It correctly identifies the ambient space UC_b(R,R), the second-order differential operator with variable coefficients, the bounded/uniformly continuous coefficient regime, the uniform ellipticity condition a(x)\ge a_0>0, the demand for a Chernoff function S(t) that is explicit rather than defined through the unknown semigroup, and the desire for convergence faster than the usual polynomial rates discussed in the comments to Problem 30.
missing_details: The paper frames this as an existence-or-impossibility problem: one should either construct such an explicit family S or prove that no meaningful such example exists.
The operator is first defined on a dense core of UC_b(R,R), namely the space of bounded smooth real-valued functions on R whose derivatives of all orders are bounded, and only then closed.
The unknown to be found is a family S:[0,\infty)\to \mathcal{L}(UC_b(R,R)) of everywhere-defined bounded linear operators, not just an unspecified approximation scheme.
The paper explicitly requires the formula for S(t) to be free of circulus vitiosus: it may not use e^{tL} in any hidden way.
The paper's comments distinguish ordinary, fast, and super-fast convergence; the question should tie the requested rate to that terminology rather than only mention one bound.
The time quantifier in the exponential-rate claim is not specified in your draft; a stand-alone question should say whether the estimate is for each fixed t>0 or uniform on compact time intervals.

As written, the inequality ||e^{tL}f-S(t/n)^n f||\le M/q^n for all f in a dense linear subspace D is not homogeneous under scalar multiplication unless some normalization or D-dependent seminorm is made explicit; this needs clarification in a fully stand-alone formulation.

The paper contains an informal/formal mismatch: the informal sentence says 'first-order differential operator with variable coefficients', but the formal statement immediately below is clearly about the second-order operator af''+bf'+cf; the refined question should follow the formal statement.
refined_question: Let X=UC_b(R,\mathbb{R}) be the Banach space of bounded uniformly continuous real-valued functions on \mathbb{R}, with the supremum norm, and let D_0 be the dense subspace of all bounded C^\infty-functions on \mathbb{R} whose derivatives of every order are bounded. Let a,b,c\in X be arbitrary real-valued functions with a(x)\ge a_0>0 for all x\in\mathbb{R}, and define on D_0 the differential operator (Lf)(x)=a(x)f''(x)+b(x)f'(x)+c(x)f(x). It is known that the closure \overline{L} generates a C_0-semigroup (e^{t\overline{L}})_{t\ge 0} on X. Does there exist a family S:[0,\infty)\to \mathcal{L}(X) of everywhere-defined bounded linear operators, given by an explicit formula depending directly on a, b, c, f, and x and containing no hidden use of the unknown semigroup (e^{t\overline{L}})_{t\ge 0}, such that S is Chernoff-equivalent to (e^{t\overline{L}})_{t\ge 0} and the Chernoff approximations S(t/n)^n converge to e^{t\overline{L}} at least exponentially fast in n on a dense linear subspace of X? If not, can one prove that no such meaningful explicit example exists?
justification: This paper does not have a relevant Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 chain for your draft; the draft clearly targets Section 7, Problem 30. The match is especially strong because Problem 30 asks for an explicit Chernoff approximation with no circular dependence on the semigroup and with super-fast (in particular, at least exponential) convergence. I followed the formal statement rather than the preceding informal sentence, because the formal statement is the precise one and it is explicitly about the second-order operator af''+bf'+cf on UC_b(R,R), which is exactly the operator class your draft uses. I also narrowed the rewrite to the paper's actual intent by keeping the problem as an existence-or-impossibility question about a practically usable explicit Chernoff family, rather than broadening it into a general approximation-rate problem.
